title.narrative: Mali Rural Electrification Hybrid System Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Rural Electrification Hybrid System Project for Mali is to expand access to modern energy services in rural areas of the recipient and to increase renewable energy generation in target areas. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is service improvement and extension of existing mini-grids. This component will increase renewable energy generation capacity in existing rural power stations supplying rural mini grids and expand those mini-grids, through: addition of approximately 4.8 MWp of capacity through hybrid systems, including photovoltaic panels, inverters, batteries and control electronics, and mini-grid extension and densification. The second component of the project is development of off-grid lighting markets and energy efficiency. This component aims to: catalyze the markets for off-grid lighting and solar lanterns in targeted rural areas, and improve energy efficiency and promote a rational and efficient use of electricity on targeted mini-grids. The third component of the project is project management support and capacity building. This component supports project management and implementation, capacity building and technical assistance to rural energy sector stakeholders, monitoring and evaluation.
The objective of the Project is to expand access to modern energy services in rural areas of the Recipient and to increase renewable energy generation in target areas.

title.narrative: Annual generation of electricity from renewable energies (solar)

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Partially Achieved</strong>. Annual electricity production as of 12/29/2023 is 10,749 MWh from the hybridizations, 1,860 MWh from Solar Home systems, and 2,165 MWh equivalent from the 98,853 solar lanterns</p>

title.narrative: Solar lanterns distributed in schools and socio-community infrastructures in non-electrified rural areas

comment.narrative:
<p>11,000 lanterns and domestic solar kits certified “Lighting Africa” were distributed to schools and socio-community infrastructures in non-electrified rural areas against a target of 10,800.</p>
<p> </p>

<p><strong>Largely exceeded</strong>: A total of 13,945 tons CO2 in 2023 derived from CDM Emission factor of 0.8kg/kWh applied to hybridization diesel emissions (8,600 tons); plus, equivalent reductions of CO2 from SHS (1,494 tons), 1,732 tons from solar lanterns, and 2,119 tons from diesel reductions from LED distributions.</p>

title.narrative: Distribution lines constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded:</strong> 227 km of MV/LV distribution lines built compared to a forecast of 225 km, which is a performance rate of 101%.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to electricity under the project by household connections - other renewable energy - off grid

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded. </strong>Out of a forecast of 550,800, around 632,147people have access to electricity thanks to domestic connections – other renewable energies – outside the networks, or 115%. The calculation methodology was based on the number of subscribers (network + SHS) multiplied by the size of the household in rural areas of 10.83 people per household = (49,060 + 9,310) x 10.83 = 632,147. This 15% excess results from the enthusiasm created by the improvement in quality and duration of service as well as the reduction in the price of kWh thanks to hybridization, among beneficiaries.</p>
<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: 45 solar/diesel hybrid power plants completed compared to a forecast of 42 power plants, i.e. an achievement rate of 107%.</p>

title.narrative: Localities reached by information and communication campaigns

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>. All localities housing a solar power plant were reached out by the information and communication campaign.</p>

title.narrative: Number of persons trained under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Largely Exceeded: </strong> 577 people benefited from training and capacity building in the fields of technical and solar engineering, management, environmental and social management, out of a forecast of 420, i.e. an execution rate of 151.19%</p> <p> </p>

title.narrative: Number of Energy efficient equipment for social infrastructure distributed

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded:  </strong>58 solar systems and energy-saving equipment were distributed as part of the productive use of solar energy for the creation of Income Generating Activities for the benefit of women in rural areas.</p>

title.narrative: Generation Capacity of Renewable Energy (other than hydropower) constructed

comment.narrative: <p>With a 7.215 kW of renewable energy production capacity (other than hydroelectricity) installed compared to a forecast of 6.18, the performance is a growth rate of 116.75%. This rate is explained by the completion of the PV/Diesel power plants whose achievements were uncertain following the restructuring of the project. The extension of the closing date made it possible to finalize all the plants.</p>

title.narrative: Studies related to rural electrification completed

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>. 9 studies related to rural electrification were carried out against a forecast of 6, i.e. a rate of 130%. Reports of all studies are available.</p>

<p><strong>Partially Achieved</strong>: 9,272 additional connections to existing mini networks compared to a forecast of 9,770, representing a performance rate of 95%.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Number of Solar Home systems installed

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: 8,554 domestic solar systems were installed, exceeding the target of 6,860, which is a completion rate of 125%.</p>

title.narrative: Number of CFLs or LEDs distributed

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Largely exceeded</strong>. 94,876 energy-saving CFL/LED bulbs distributed in rural areas compared to a forecast of 58,700 or 162%.</p>

<p><strong>Partially Achieved</strong>: 98,853 “Lighting Africa” certified domestic solar lanterns and kits were distributed through 15 national distributors, based on the Results-Based Financing Mechanism (RBF), compared to a forecast of 90,000, which a performance rate of 110%.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Project related grievances registered under the project grievance redress mechanism (GRM) and addressed

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>. 9 complaints registered and all of which were handled to the satisfaction of the complainants.</p>
